entities.name: Benzyl aryl ether substrate
observations: Contains an aryl O–CH2–phenyl benzyl ether.
Source assignment and transformation evidence supplied by search agent.

entities.name: Phenolic product
observations: Corresponds to cleavage of the aryl O–CH2–phenyl group to give Ar–OH; fused heterocycle and stereocenter are retained.

entities.name: Hydrogenolytic debenzylation
observations: Transformation: aryl benzyl ether Ar–O–CH2Ph to phenol Ar–OH.
Most strongly matching empirical conditions use Pd/C in ethanol with a hydrogen source; associated record includes dichloromethane, 3.0 h, and 19.9% yield.
Hydrogen gas was not explicitly listed in the record, so H2 is chemically inferred rather than directly recorded.

entities.name: Pd/C ethanol hydrogenolysis
observations: Palladium on carbon in ethanol is the strongest supported reagent system for this debenzylation.
Typical practical hydrogen source is H2; transfer-hydrogen alternatives include ammonium formate or cyclohexene, but those alternatives are interpretive.
Associated empirical record: approximately 3.0 h and 19.9% yield; dichloromethane appears as a record-associated solvent/component.
